reason: Session settled the naming of refs and their placement on the map: @ always reads address first, a ref is a stable record with a unique ref_id named address@ref_id, and files are placed by an agent's explicit link rather than automatic matching. Held tickets code.graph.knowledge#c and code.analyzer.refactoring#1a depend on this, and no skill records it yet.

Linking a file to an element is now a dispatch verb (dispatch_link), and the obvious alternative, map knowledge add-element with refs, silently replaces an element's sources refs. The skill must steer agents to the safe call and away from the destructive one.

An agent editing a CHANGELOG and test file hit the file-access gate; the refusal text says the link must come first. This skill covers linking but not that the gate blocks edits until the link exists, so an agent would otherwise learn it from a refusal.
The ref form changed this session: the id leads and the join closes the name. The old address-first form in this skill is now wrong and would mislead agents naming refs.
The code-link path and the automatic matcher were removed this session; the skill still tells agents to use a removed verb.
Status line goes stale as tickets move; record the state as of this date and keep the rule to read the ticket first.
The episode bypassed the link gate by editing through a script and linked only afterwards; the skill covers the Edit tool but not scripted writes, and its dated status line is stale.

Owner ruled on 2026-10-15 that refs are not properties and never move; this skill still states the CTX-009 moving rule for refs, which is now superseded. Also records that role-less elements created for refs break the page tree.

Rich corrected an agent that moved refs to a common prefix and called it the transitive rule; the existing line 13 states the ruling but does not forbid the transitivity justification that produced the bug.

The agent wrote a new draft file under artifacts/specs-draft/ with no link. The Write was refused, then the gate's unlock message arrived and dispatch_link fixed it. The skill implies only existing files; new files need the same link first, which saves a refused write.
The ref skill's status line says an old process still moves refs, but gives no way to check it. Pointing at the new process-restart skill keeps the warning actionable.

code.graph.knowledge#17 made linking an already-linked file at a second place write a second ref with a derived name. The skill's uniqueness rule reads as if such a link is refused, which would mislead the next agent about the name it gets back.

An agent linked flow.js at a made-up child Address (code.interface.graphical.flow); the link created an empty element holding one ref, which the page drew as a node. The skill forbids making elements for refs but does not say that a link at a new Address creates one, nor the safe undo order.

A dispatch_link with a hyphenated, spaced title ref was refused; the retry with a period-and-underscore name linked. The refusal rule and its accepted form belong in the ref naming rule so the first attempt is right.

A worker's dispatch_link for artifacts/specs-draft/...md was refused because the ref was the spaced title 'STORE-029 runner hand-over draft'; the retry with a dotted ref_id linked the file. The rule about ref_id form was implicit and the worker had to learn it by failing.
Absorbed into metaform-map-knowledge: ref naming and file links are its refs section, with the detail in references/ref-links.md.
